extracted.intended_audience: foundation staff and policymakers; minority organizations seeking foundation support; researchers of philanthropy and grantmaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance, survey instruments, findings and recommendations for assessing and improving how private foundations respond to Hispanic needs (grantmaking patterns, institutional policies, applicant support, and data collection). Useful for foundations, applicants, and researchers studying philanthropic responsiveness to minorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to foundation guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants do not study and/or adhere to foundation’s guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposals for whether applicants read and follow a foundation's stated application rules and procedures. Anti-pattern: submitting proposals that ignore stated length, format, deadlines, or required content. Scoring note: lack of adherence is flagged as a common weakness reducing likelihood of funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal contents and structure quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal contents and structure of minority applicants is poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess proposals for clear, well-organized content and an appropriate structure (goals, methods, budget, evaluation). Examples of weakness include vague objectives, missing sections, or disorganized presentation. Guidance suggests foundations could offer technical assistance to improve proposal quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of management, budgeting, and fundraising capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Minority applicants do not evidence efficient management, budgeting and fund-raising capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate applicants on demonstrated organizational capacity: realistic budgets, administrative systems, fundraising strategy, and prior management experience. Lack of such evidence is cited as a barrier to receiving foundation support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant research on target foundations
rubrics_metrics.description: Minority applicants do not conduct research on target foundations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: whether applicants have researched a foundation's interests, past grants, and fit. Anti-pattern: sending generic proposals without tailoring to foundation priorities. Scoring guidance: better-researched, targeted proposals score higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of available technical assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Minority applicants do not request and use available technical assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether applicants seek and apply available proposal-writing help, feedback, or other technical assistance. Foundations are encouraged to publicize and provide such assistance; applicants who use it are considered stronger candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Hispanic and minority mailing lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Large foundations should have an Hispanic and other minorities mailing list. If not possible, include a representative group of Hispanic and other minority agencies, institutions and organizations in regular mailing lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metric for foundation outreach/communication: existence and scope of mailing lists targeted to minority organizations. Guidance: mailing lists increase visibility to minority applicants; lack thereof is a recommended area for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to mail and inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should accept the responsibility of reading their mail and responding to letters received in a more serious manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate foundation practices on timely, substantive responses to inquiries and correspondence. Scoring: responsiveness (e.g., written responses to negative decisions, timely replies) is a positive institutional practice; failure to respond is criticized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility to minority program developers
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should seek ways to be more visible to minority groups developing programs in their fields of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess outreach efforts (publicity, community visits, networks) aimed at making foundations known to minority-led organizations. Guidance: proactive visibility increases minority applicants' awareness and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate evaluation criteria (not blind equality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations evaluating proposals should consider more appropriate criteria rather than being blindly ‘fair’ by giving equal treatment to potential applicants of unequal strength and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for foundation grant review: evaluate applicants relative to capacity and context rather than applying identical standards that disadvantage less-resourced groups. Guidance suggests providing compensatory support (e.g., technical assistance) when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget allocation for applicant information and technical assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should devote a small part of their operating budget to offer timely information and technical assistance to minority applicants, particularly in the area of proposal writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metric: presence of an allocated budget line or program for applicant assistance. Examples: workshops, advisory services, draft feedback. Scoring: foundations that fund assistance are rated higher for supportiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written affirmative action plan for staff and boards
rubrics_metrics.description: Each foundation should set forth in writing an affirmative action plan for increased representation of women and minorities on its staff and Board of Directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether foundations have formal, documented plans to increase diversity among staff and trustees. Guidance: written plans (with targets/timelines) are preferred; absence indicates a need for institutional change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant data extraction fields (FGI card)
rubrics_metrics.description: Card designed to extract grant information from the Foundation Grants Index: fields include (1) identification number, (2) Hispanic Group, (3) Amount, (4) Date, (5) Grantee, (6) Information Source, (7) Foundation Name, (8) Address, (9) Contact Person, (10) Telephone No., (11) Category, (12) Purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a data-collection rubric for researchers cataloging grants. Guidance: 'Category' should be a broad field label (e.g., Education, Health); 'Purpose' should be verbatim transcription from FGI. Suggested revisions: add a field for 'Grantee Board of Directors' (to record whether grantee's board is at least 50% minority controlled) and add a sub-category field for grants analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey metrics for classifying foundations and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Questionnaire items to characterize foundations: type of foundation (general purpose, company-sponsored, community, family, special purpose, other), assets (less than $1M; $1–$25M; $26–$100M; over $100M), total dollar amount of grants (categories), average grant size (categories), presence and size of full-time staff, publications (annual/biennial/multi-annual/brochure), Hispanic mailing list (yes/no/do not know), inclusion policy for mailing list, responsiveness to letters, and information provided to prospective applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these items as institutional metrics to evaluate and compare foundations' capacity and openness. 'Information provided to applicants' subitems include: application deadlines; specific suggestions for proposal contents; length; format; dates when Executive Board meets; feedback on preliminary drafts or concept papers; advice on other funding sources. These items form a standardized rubric for assessing foundation transparency and applicant supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure board and staff Hispanic representation and consultant use
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported metrics used: percent of foundations with persons of Hispanic origin serving as directors/trustees, percent employing full-time persons of Hispanic origin, percent using Hispanic consultants, percent having a Hispanic mailing list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional diversity metrics: collect and evaluate board composition (count and ethnicity), staff demographics, consultant usage, and communications lists. Use these as indicators of foundation sensitivity and accessibility to Hispanic communities; low percentages indicate limited engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantmaking distribution and concentration metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings and implied metrics: percent of total foundation dollars awarded to Hispanics vs. population share; concentration of grants (e.g., few large grants account for a high share); number of grants per foundation; share of grants to Hispanic-controlled agencies; regional distribution; distribution by field of interest (education, civil rights/legal services, research, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these quantitative metrics to evaluate foundations' substantive support for Hispanic needs: compare percent funding to population share; measure concentration (share of dollars in top grants), distribution across recipient agency control (Hispanic-controlled vs non-Hispanic), and field-by-field allocation. Scoring: more even, representative, and sustained funding patterns score higher for responsiveness.
